text(await tools.exec_command({cmd:"cat > /tmp/exposed-preferred-design-sol.md <<'EOF'
## Problem

Reviewed family labels must become explicit pipeline policy rather than whichever source name happens to have the smallest UUID. Identity still comes from the smallest UUID after all alias and family joins. Recorded names, aliases, kinds, company data, direct evidence, member history, and group membership must stay unchanged. An alias bridge can make an unrelated funder the representative; a reviewed family can contain only one stored identity; multiple reviewed families can land in one final component.

## Usage (caller’s view)

The policy JSON adds `preferred_name` to each family: BBC, GB News, Premier League. Operators run the existing refresh command or ingestion pipeline; HTTP search and funder details then use the projected label.

```rust
let projection = build_funder_groups(&snapshot)?; // includes preferred names
replace_funder_groups(&mut tx).await?; // same atomic writer
let matches = db.get_funders_by_text_search_score(&request).await?;
// Query BBC, result id remains minimum UUID, name is BBC.
let details = db.funder_funding(recorded_member_id).await?;
// Profile uses BBC; requested id and all funding aggregation retain current contracts.
```

No new public repository method or HTTP field is required.

## Shape

Use a sparse group-name metadata table, containing one row only for components with an unambiguous reviewed-family name. Fallback display remains the representative's recorded source name. This avoids copying every fallback name and preserves existing behavior before first refresh and in fixtures without a refresh.

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Deserialize)]
#[serde(try_from = "String")]
struct PreferredFunderName(String); // parse trim; reject empty; retain display spelling
impl TryFrom<String> for PreferredFunderName { /* Policy error on blank */ }
impl PreferredFunderName { fn as_str(&self) -> &str { /* ... */ } }

#[derive(Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
struct ReviewedFamily {
    key: String,
    preferred_name: PreferredFunderName,
    names: Vec<String>,
}
struct PreferredGroupName {
    group_id: FunderId,
    name: PreferredFunderName,
}
pub struct FunderGroups {
    memberships: Vec<(FunderId, FunderId)>,
    preferred_names: Vec<PreferredGroupName>,
    alias_links: Vec<FunderAliasLink>,
    family_links: Vec<FunderFamilyLink>,
}
// New error variant: AmbiguousPreferredName { group_id: Uuid, family_keys: Vec<String> }
```

Keep all new types in `domain/models/funder_grouping.rs`, fields crate-visible only where persistence needs them. The parsed preferred name owns the nonempty rule. Family membership still matches reviewed canonical source names only, never aliases or preferred display labels. Store family matched IDs during the existing family loop, including singleton matches, independently of pairwise family-link creation. After every union has finished, map each matched ID to its final root and build `BTreeMap<Uuid, BTreeMap<family_key, preferred_name>>`. Zero families means fallback, one means projected name, more than one rejects the refresh with a deterministic error. Reject even equal labels for distinct families: label equality does not authorize ownership selection. This prevents accidental arbitrary labeling while retaining the last valid atomic projection.

Migration (new reversible pair only):

```sql
CREATE TABLE exposed.funder_group_names (
    group_id uuid PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES exposed.funders(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    preferred_name text NOT NULL CHECK (btrim(preferred_name) <> '')
);
CREATE INDEX funder_group_names_preferred_trgm
ON exposed.funder_group_names USING gin (preferred_name gin_trgm_ops);
-- down: DROP TABLE exposed.funder_group_names;
```

The existing advisory-locked transaction computes the entire domain projection first, deletes old name rows along with existing memberships/evidence, and inserts new name rows using `sqlx::query!`. Policy failure occurs before deletes; database failure rolls everything back. Refresh twice gives the same rows. No migration embeds family names or policy selection SQL; the pipeline remains the sole policy owner. Existing installations apply migration then run refresh without ingestion replay.

Read naming everywhere using the same simple expression:

```sql
LEFT JOIN exposed.funder_group_names n ON n.group_id = representative.id
COALESCE(n.preferred_name, representative.funder_name) AS name
```

Use this in text result grouping, phonetic result display, and the `funder_funding` profile query. Member history continues selecting stored `f.funder_name` directly. Do not change kind inference or member/company aggregation.

Text search must score preferred labels as actual candidates, not merely display them after old-source qualification. Preserve the recorded candidate/scored branches and add a compatible preferred branch:

```sql
SELECT n.group_id AS id, n.preferred_name AS candidate_name,
       NULL::text AS matched_alias,
       word_similarity($1, n.preferred_name) AS similarity_score
FROM exposed.funder_group_names n
WHERE n.preferred_name %> $1
  AND word_similarity($1, n.preferred_name) >= $2
```

Union this with qualified recorded hits before the group winner/limit stage. Carry a boolean `preferred_candidate` into winner selection. Highest similarity remains first; prefer a preferred-name candidate on equal score, then retain existing stable identity tie-breakers. Preferred candidates report `SearchMatchSource::Name`. For recorded candidates, derive final provenance against the displayed name, not only UUID: `CASE WHEN matched_alias IS NOT NULL THEN matched_alias WHEN candidate_name <> display_name THEN candidate_name END`. This fixes representative-source provenance when the representative itself is renamed. A nonrepresentative recorded canonical equal to the display name may report Name consistently; if preserving current alias provenance is required, retain the existing different-id clause as well. Recommended smallest behavioral change: alias if different ID OR different display name, preferred candidates explicitly Name.

Phonetic search remains restricted to individuals; this task adds no family label phonetic candidate semantics. It must nevertheless use the projected display expression and mark a representative recorded candidate as Alias if its spelling differs from the display label. This keeps provenance truthful even for an individual pulled into a reviewed family by an alias bridge.

This public surface is unchanged; policy parsing, final-component resolution, conflict detection, and persistence are hidden inside the existing grouping boundary. Read queries need only a name join and candidate contribution, per boundary-discipline and single-source-of-truth.

## Synthesis decision

Candidate recommendation: sparse persisted metadata, final-component resolution, and explicit conflict failure.

## Tradeoffs accepted

- We accept one table and join in exchange for no duplicated names on N membership rows and no runtime policy interpretation.
- We accept refresh refusal for cross-family components in exchange for never presenting an arbitrarily selected reviewed label. The old complete projection survives.
- We accept the existing representative kind even when the label changes in exchange for keeping this task scoped to naming policy.

## Alternatives considered

- Name on every membership: simpler joins but repeats one invariant across many rows and permits disagreement within a group. Reads must decide which row's name to trust; updates must synchronize redundant values.
- Full metadata row for every component: centralizes all names, but copies fallback source names and requires backfill or fallback while offering no needed capability beyond sparse preferred labels.
- Runtime policy lookup: avoids migration but leaks policy matching/final-component rules into multiple readers, cannot naturally provide indexed preferred-name candidate search, and can disagree with stored membership after policy changes.

## Implementation reconciliation

None yet.

## Open questions and risks

No user answer is needed for implementation. Conflict refusal is explicit and testable; if later product requirements demand cross-family labels, that requires a reviewed composite naming policy rather than UUID or family-key precedence.

## Verification

Domain tests: each family preferred label independent of UUID/input order; singleton canonical family member gets preferred label despite zero family evidence; preferred label absent from recorded names; unrelated smallest-ID alias bridge still gets label; aliases alone do not activate a reviewed family; blank preferred names fail parsing; two families in final component fail deterministically; grouping memberships and evidence remain unchanged.

SQLx integration: preferred exact query at threshold 1 returns one group with stable ID even without exact recorded label; old recorded and alias queries return preferred label and truthful provenance; representative source differing from label reports Alias; preferred candidate ties report Name; requested member funder details retain requested ID but preferred name; member history and recorded aliases remain unchanged; repeated refresh and failed ambiguous refresh preserve atomic rows. Migration test forward existing data plus down/up isolated database. Real API verification: one BBC result, 12 grouped source identities, 71 funding entries, plus GB News and Premier League names and recorded-name queries.

## Next implementation step

Add typed policy preferred names and final-component metadata with domain tests, then create the migration and wire the existing atomic projection/readers.
